name: client-16c
description: Hypothetical 16-core client-SoC NPU in the class of the 16-core Neural Engine Apple states for M4 (38 trillion operations per second, precision not stated; 120GB/s memory bandwidth). 16 cores of 32x32 output-stationary arrays: 16384 MAC/cycle, 39.3216 TOP/s at 1.2 GHz and 2 ops/MAC, 3.5% above 38. The 1.2 GHz clock makes 120 GB/s exactly 100 B/cycle; that rate is the whole SoC's, shared with the CPU and GPU. Per core: SRAM 256 KiB, sized by the S10 rule as Apple publishes no Neural Engine SRAM size: the smallest power of two from 64 KiB to 4 MiB at which ResNet-50 and MobileNetV2 each reach 90% of their highest MAC utilisation in the sweep, on this point and on workstation-32c, which shares the core; one 256-bit AXI port, the narrowest width at which the read channels of the 32 cores of workstation-32c reach its DRAM rate; Vela 5.2.0 Ethos-U85 DRAM latencies (500 read, 250 write cycles) and outstanding limits (64 reads, 32 writes); bursts up to 8 beats, the shortest power of two with which 64 outstanding reads cover 500 cycles; depthwise datapath 128 MAC/cycle by the S9 rule, as Apple publishes no Neural Engine microarchitecture to take a rate from: the smallest power of two at which MobileNetV2 runs within 5% of its latency with a depthwise datapath as wide as the array. Tiles 64x64x256 by the mobile-2k rule (panels at least 128 B deep); the 89600 B left over is the weight cache. Partition auto. Pipeline 4 cycles per panel, the simulator default.
